45: 
46: /**
47:  */
48: public class ArithmeticPostAggregator implements PostAggregator
49: {
50:   public static final Comparator DEFAULT_COMPARATOR = DoubleSumAggregator.COMPARATOR;
51: 
52:   private final String name;
53:   private final String fnName;
54:   private final List<PostAggregator> fields;
55:   private final Ops op;
56:   private final Comparator comparator;
57:   private final String ordering;
58: 
59:   public ArithmeticPostAggregator(
60:       String name,
61:       String fnName,
62:       List<PostAggregator> fields
63:   )
64:   {
65:     this(name, fnName, fields, null);
66:   }
67: 
68:   @JsonCreator
69:   public ArithmeticPostAggregator(
70:       @JsonProperty("name") String name,
71:       @JsonProperty("fn") String fnName,
72:       @JsonProperty("fields") List<PostAggregator> fields,
73:       @JsonProperty("ordering") @Nullable String ordering
74:   )
75:   {
76:     Preconditions.checkArgument(fnName != null, "fn cannot not be null");
77:     Preconditions.checkArgument(fields != null && fields.size() > 1, "Illegal number of fields[%s], must be > 1");
78: 
79:     this.name = name;
80:     this.fnName = fnName;
81:     this.fields = fields;
82: 
83:     this.op = Ops.lookup(fnName);
84:     if (op == null) {
85:       throw new IAE("Unknown operation[%s], known operations[%s]", fnName, Ops.getFns());
86:     }
87: 
88:     this.ordering = ordering;
89:     this.comparator = ordering == null ? DEFAULT_COMPARATOR : Ordering.valueOf(ordering);
90:   }
91: 
92:   @Override
93:   public Set<String> getDependentFields()
94:   {
95:     Set<String> dependentFields = new HashSet<>();
96:     for (PostAggregator field : fields) {
97:       dependentFields.addAll(field.getDependentFields());
98:     }
99:     return dependentFields;
100:   }
101: 
102:   @Override
103:   public Comparator getComparator()
104:   {
105:     return comparator;
106:   }
107: 
108:   @Override
109:   public Object compute(Map<String, Object> values)
110:   {
111:     Double retVal = NullHandling.replaceWithDefault() ? 0.0d : null;
112:     boolean firstOperand = true;
113:     for (PostAggregator field : fields) {
114:       Number nextVal;
115:       if (field instanceof ConstantPostAggregator) {
116:         ConstantPostAggregator constantField = (ConstantPostAggregator) field;
117:         nextVal = constantField.getConstantValue();
118:       } else if (field instanceof FieldAccessPostAggregator) {
119:         FieldAccessPostAggregator accessField = (FieldAccessPostAggregator) field;
120:         Object raw = values.get(accessField.getFieldName());
121:         if (raw == null
122:             && accessField.getName() != null
123:             && accessField.getName().equals(accessField.getFieldName())) {
124:           raw = values.get(accessField.getName());
125:         }
126:         nextVal = (Number) raw;
127:       } else if (field instanceof FinalizingFieldAccessPostAggregator) {
128:         FinalizingFieldAccessPostAggregator finalizingField = (FinalizingFieldAccessPostAggregator) field;
129:         if (finalizingField.getFinalizer() == null || finalizingField.getRawComparator() == null) {
130:           throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not decorated");
131:         }
132:         Object raw = finalizingField.getFinalizer().apply(values.get(finalizingField.getFieldName()));
133:         if (finalizingField.getFinalizedType() != null && raw instanceof Number) {
134:           nextVal = ((Number) raw).doubleValue();
135:         } else {
136:           nextVal = (Number) raw;
137:         }
138:       } else {
139:         nextVal = (Number) field.compute(values);
140:       }
141:       if (nextVal == null) {
142:         // As per SQL standard if any of the value is null, arithmetic operators will return null.
143:         return null;
144:       }
145:       if (firstOperand) {
146:         retVal = nextVal.doubleValue();
147:         firstOperand = false;
148:       } else {
149:         retVal = op.compute(retVal, nextVal.doubleValue());
150:       }
151:     }
152:     return retVal;
153:   }
154: 
155:   @Override
156:   @JsonProperty
157:   public String getName()
158:   {
159:     return name;
160:   }
161: 
162:   @Override
163:   public ColumnType getType(ColumnInspector signature)
164:   {
165:     return ColumnType.DOUBLE;
166:   }
167: 
168:   @Override
169:   public ArithmeticPostAggregator decorate(Map<String, AggregatorFactory> aggregators)
170:   {
171:     return new ArithmeticPostAggregator(name, fnName, Queries.decoratePostAggregators(fields, aggregators), ordering);
172:   }
173: 
174:   @Override
175:   public byte[] getCacheKey()
176:   {
177:     final CacheKeyBuilder builder = new CacheKeyBuilder(PostAggregatorIds.ARITHMETIC)
178:         .appendString(fnName)
179:         .appendString(ordering);
180: 
181:     if (preserveFieldOrderInCacheKey(op)) {
182:       builder.appendCacheables(fields);
183:     } else {
184:       builder.appendCacheablesIgnoringOrder(fields);
185:     }
186: 
187:     return builder.build();
188:   }

190:   @JsonProperty("fn")
191:   public String getFnName()
192:   {
193:     return fnName;
194:   }

196:   @JsonProperty("ordering")
197:   @JsonInclude(Include.NON_NULL)
198:   public String getOrdering()
199:   {
200:     return ordering;
201:   }
202: 
203:   @JsonProperty
204:   public List<PostAggregator> getFields()
205:   {
206:     return fields;
207:   }
208: 
209:   @Override
210:   public String toString()
211:   {
212:     return "ArithmeticPostAggregator{" +
213:            "name='" + name + '\'' +
214:            ", fnName='" + fnName + '\'' +
215:            ", fields=" + fields +
216:            ", op=" + op +
217:            '}';
218:   }
219: 
220:   private static boolean preserveFieldOrderInCacheKey(Ops op)
221:   {
222:     switch (op) {
223:       case PLUS:
224:       case MULT:
225:         return false;
226:       case MINUS:
227:       case DIV:
228:       case QUOTIENT:
229:         return true;
230:       default:
231:         throw new IAE(op.fn);
232:     }
233:   }
234: 
235:   private enum Ops
236:   {
237:     PLUS("+") {
238:       @Override
239:       public double compute(double lhs, double rhs)
240:       {
241:         return lhs + rhs;
242:       }
243:     },
244:     MINUS("-") {
245:       @Override
246:       public double compute(double lhs, double rhs)
247:       {
248:         return lhs - rhs;
249:       }
250:     },
251:     MULT("*") {
252:       @Override
253:       public double compute(double lhs, double rhs)
254:       {
255:         return lhs * rhs;
256:       }
257:     },
258:     DIV("/") {
259:       @Override
260:       public double compute(double lhs, double rhs)
261:       {
262:         return (rhs == 0.0) ? 0 : (lhs / rhs);
263:       }
264:     },
265:     QUOTIENT("quotient") {
266:       @Override
267:       public double compute(double lhs, double rhs)
268:       {
269:         return lhs / rhs;
270:       }
271:     };
272: 
273:     private static final Map<String, Ops> LOOKUP_MAP = new HashMap<>();
274: 
275:     static {
276:       for (Ops op : Ops.values()) {
277:         LOOKUP_MAP.put(op.getFn(), op);
278:       }
279:     }
280: 
281:     private final String fn;
282: 
283:     Ops(String fn)
284:     {
285:       this.fn = fn;
286:     }
287: 
288:     public String getFn()
289:     {
290:       return fn;
291:     }
292: 
293:     public abstract double compute(double lhs, double rhs);
294: 
295:     static Ops lookup(String fn)
296:     {
297:       return LOOKUP_MAP.get(fn);
298:     }
299: 
300:     static Set<String> getFns()
301:     {
302:       return LOOKUP_MAP.keySet();
303:     }
304:   }
305: 
306:   public enum Ordering implements Comparator<Double>
307:   {
308:     /**
309:      * Ensures the following order: numeric > NaN > Infinite.
310:      *
311:      * The name may be referenced via {@link #valueOf(String)} in the constructor {@link
312:      * ArithmeticPostAggregator#ArithmeticPostAggregator(String, String, List, String)}.
313:      */
314:     @SuppressWarnings("unused")
315:     numericFirst {
316:       @Override
317:       public int compare(Double lhs, Double rhs)
318:       {
319:         if (Double.isFinite(lhs) && !Double.isFinite(rhs)) {
320:           return 1;
321:         }
322:         if (!Double.isFinite(lhs) && Double.isFinite(rhs)) {
323:           return -1;
324:         }
325:         return Double.compare(lhs, rhs);
326:       }
327:     }
328:   }
329: 
330:   @Override
331:   public boolean equals(Object o)
332:   {
333:     if (this == o) {
334:       return true;
335:     }
336:     if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) {
337:       return false;
338:     }
339: 
340:     ArithmeticPostAggregator that = (ArithmeticPostAggregator) o;
341: 
342:     if (!comparator.equals(that.comparator)) {
343:       return false;
344:     }
345:     if (!fields.equals(that.fields)) {
346:       return false;
347:     }
348:     if (!fnName.equals(that.fnName)) {
349:       return false;
350:     }
351:     if (name != null ? !name.equals(that.name) : that.name != null) {
352:       return false;
353:     }
354:     if (op != that.op) {
355:       return false;
356:     }
357:     if (ordering != null ? !ordering.equals(that.ordering) : that.ordering != null) {
358:       return false;
359:     }
360: 
361:     return true;
362:   }
363: 
364:   @Override
365:   public int hashCode()
366:   {
367:     int result = name != null ? name.hashCode() : 0;
368:     result = 31 * result + fnName.hashCode();
369:     result = 31 * result + fields.hashCode();
370:     result = 31 * result + op.hashCode();
371:     result = 31 * result + comparator.hashCode();
372:     result = 31 * result + (ordering != null ? ordering.hashCode() : 0);
373:     return result;
374:   }
375: }

> Apache Druid supports two query languages: [Druid SQL](sql.md) and [native queries](querying.md).
> This document describes the native
> language. For information about functions available in SQL, refer to the
> [SQL documentation](sql-aggregations.md).

Post-aggregations are specifications of processing that should happen on aggregated values as they come out of Apache Druid. If you include a post aggregation as part of a query, make sure to include all aggregators the post-aggregator requires.

There are several post-aggregators available.

### Arithmetic post-aggregator

The arithmetic post-aggregator applies the provided function to the given
fields from left to right. The fields can be aggregators or other post aggregators.

Supported functions are `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, and `quotient`.

**Note**:

* `/` division always returns `0` if dividing by`0`, regardless of the numerator.
* `quotient` division behaves like regular floating point division
* Arithmetic post-aggregators always use floating point arithmetic.

Arithmetic post-aggregators may also specify an `ordering`, which defines the order
of resulting values when sorting results (this can be useful for topN queries for instance):

- If no ordering (or `null`) is specified, the default floating point ordering is used.
- `numericFirst` ordering always returns finite values first, followed by `NaN`, and infinite values last.

The grammar for an arithmetic post aggregation is:

```json
postAggregation : {
  "type"  : "arithmetic",
  "name"  : <output_name>,
  "fn"    : <arithmetic_function>,
  "fields": [<post_aggregator>, <post_aggregator>, ...],
  "ordering" : <null (default), or "numericFirst">
}
```

### Field accessor post-aggregators

These post-aggregators return the value produced by the specified [aggregator](../querying/aggregations.md).

`fieldName` refers to the output name of the aggregator given in the [aggregations](../querying/aggregations.md) portion of the query.
For complex aggregators, like "cardinality" and "hyperUnique", the `type` of the post-aggregator determines what
the post-aggregator will return. Use type "fieldAccess" to return the raw aggregation object, or use type
"finalizingFieldAccess" to return a finalized value, such as an estimated cardinality.

```json
{ "type" : "fieldAccess", "name": <output_name>, "fieldName" : <aggregator_name> }
```

or

```json
{ "type" : "finalizingFieldAccess", "name": <output_name>, "fieldName" : <aggregator_name> }
```


### Constant post-aggregator

The constant post-aggregator always returns the specified value.

```json
{ "type"  : "constant", "name"  : <output_name>, "value" : <numerical_value> }
